A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same online SNN framework, renamed from EM-PF to HM-DF. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification results in Table 2, SECA ablations in Table 3, and training/inference-speed experiments in Figure 4.

after.justification: V2 reports original classification and SECA results in Tables 2–3, plus accuracy and synaptic-operation experiments in Figure 3.

M1.justification: The neuron firing/reset equations and main online-learning procedures survive the renaming. V2 adds a 1.5-bit ternary-weight option alongside binary weights and removes Sign binarization between GAP and Conv1d in SECA (v1 Eq. 9; v2 Eq. 8). These are limited but actual procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-200, ImageNet-1k, and DVS-CIFAR10. Replacing the ImageNet-200 SECA ablation with DVS-CIFAR10 and adding SOP measurements do not introduce new datasets, tasks, or input environments.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same comparator membership within every dataset, including the corresponding GLIF, SLTT, OTTT, and NDOT comparisons. Vanilla online learning remains the efficiency reference; the new weight-precision cases are variants of the proposed model.

E3.justification: The appendix changes the reported ImageNet-1k configuration from 120 to 300 epochs, learning rate 0.01 to 0.025, weight decay 0.0005 to zero, and binary to ternary weights. V2 also introduces accuracy-versus-convolutional-SOP evaluation across time-step settings, replacing the earlier CIFAR-10 speed-ratio experiments.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 replaces random-backpropagation and parallel-computation timing ablations with binary/ternary accuracy–SOP analyses on CIFAR-100 and DVS-CIFAR10. Table 3 retains the CIFAR-10/100 SECA ablations but removes the ImageNet-200 ablation and adds DVS-CIFAR10, substantially changing the supporting analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. Both present point estimates; batch-normalization statistics are not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes reported CIFAR-10 accuracy from 95.51% to 95.59%, CIFAR-100 from 79.91% to 78.45%, and DVS-CIFAR10/ResNet-18 from 78.10% to 81.70%. ImageNet-1k changes from 68.07% to 69.77% under revised training and precision settings, so this is not a same-setting gain. SECA outcomes are revised, including a new 83.50% DVS-CIFAR10 result, and accuracy/SOP results replace the previous speedup results.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.2 and its proof are retained; the additional silent-neuron equation merely expands the existing argument. Substantive localized corrections occur in Corollary 4.3 and the reparameterization equations: normalization thresholds change, leakage terms move outside the normalization fraction, and batch-normalization bias signs are corrected.

C1.justification: Beyond retained gradient-separability and time/memory-efficiency claims, v2 adds a central claim of strong online-learning performance without increased power consumption. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion also recast the contribution around hybrid firing/reset and explicitly foreground surrogate-gradient alignment.

C2.justification: V2 introduces a substantive energy tradeoff: binary weights incur more SOPs at matched time steps, ternary sparsity reduces this cost, and fewer time steps can provide comparable accuracy at lower cost. V1's discussion of SECA inference slowdown and its mitigation through parallel computation disappears. The interpretation of deployment efficiency consequently shifts substantially.

D1.justification: V2 adds per-experiment weight-precision assignments in Table S1, specifies convolution-only SOP accounting, and clarifies Table 2's parameter-memory scope. Conversely, v1's explicit binary quantizer, straight-through derivative, membrane-parameter gradient formulas, and deployment-binarization instruction are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature on ternary weights, neuron models, normalization, and spiking transformers. A new passage acknowledges LIAF-Net's similar model structure and distinguishes its lightweight-processing objective from online training and deployment. The overall related-work organization and principal positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, changes the author list, systematically renames EM-PF to HM-DF, revises selected explanations, and switches to numbered citations. Experimental configuration and proof subsections exchange appendix positions. Most section organization and substantial portions of the prose remain matched.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn with reset and gradient-alignment illustrations. V1 Figures 2–3 are redrawn and merged into v2 Figure 2; the speed plot is removed and an accuracy/SOP plot added. Tables gain revised styling, explanatory captions, and a weight-precision column, while appendix and algorithm layouts are reorganized.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects normalization algebra and adds useful accuracy–SOP evidence, precision settings, and positioning against LIAF-Net. However, it removes the empirical training/inference-speed validation while retaining speed claims, and its new power-consumption claims rest on convolutional SOP counts rather than measured energy. These gains and losses affect central efficiency arguments, leaving no reliably assessable net direction in overall quality.
